en: suddenly (of an idea); in a flash

examples.en: A good idea suddenly came to me while I was showering.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자 번뜩 정신이 들었어요.
examples.en: When I heard that, I snapped to my senses.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 번뜩 어제 약속이 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: In the middle of the meeting, I suddenly remembered yesterday's appointment.

examples.ko: 번뜩 고개를 들어 보니 친구가 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I looked up all of a sudden and my friend was standing there.
My eyes flew open, and it was already morning.
While solving the problem, the answer suddenly became clear.

explain: 주로 '번뜩 떠오르다', '번뜩 생각나다'처럼 어떤 생각이나 기억이 갑자기 스칠 때 써요. '번쩍'과 비슷한데, '번뜩'은 순간적으로 머리나 눈이 열리는 느낌이 더 강해요. 동사 '번뜩이다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in '번뜩 떠오르다' or '번뜩 생각나다', when a thought or memory flashes through your mind. It is close to '번쩍', but '번뜩' feels more like your mind or eyes suddenly opening. It is good to learn it together with the verb '번뜩이다'.

examples.ko: 광고 회사에서는 번뜩이는 아이디어만큼 기획력도 중요해요.
examples.en: At an ad agency, planning skills matter as much as flashes of brilliant ideas.
The cat's eyes flashed in the dark.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 눈빛이 번뜩이고 말도 빨라요.
examples.en: That student has sharp, gleaming eyes and speaks fast.
He changed the mood with a flash of wit.
The window flashed in the sunlight and dazzled my eyes.
I quickly jotted down the thought that had flashed through my head.

explain: '번뜩이는 아이디어', '번뜩이는 재치', '눈빛이 번뜩이다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요. '반짝이다'는 작은 빛이 계속 나는 느낌이고, '번뜩이다'는 순간 강하게 빛나는 느낌이에요. 아이디어나 재능이 뛰어날 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used in set phrases like '번뜩이는 아이디어' (a flash of an idea), '번뜩이는 재치' (a flash of wit), and '눈빛이 번뜩이다' (eyes gleam). '반짝이다' feels like a small light that keeps shining, while '번뜩이다' is a strong light for a moment. It can also describe brilliant ideas or talent.

examples.ko: 시험 결과 때문에 며칠 동안 번민이 깊었어요.
examples.en: I was deeply anguished for several days over the exam results.

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 번민 끝에 회사를 떠나기로 했어요.
examples.en: After long agonizing, he decided to leave the company.
After I confided in my friend, my anguish eased a little.
He was sitting there with a face full of anguish.
I walked every day to forget my torment.

examples.ko: 젊을 때는 진로 번민이 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: When you are young, everyone has worries about their career path.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 보통 '고민'이라고 말하고, '번민'은 글이나 이야기에서 마음이 아주 괴로울 때 써요. '번민에 빠지다', '번민이 깊다'처럼 자주 써요. 동사는 '번민하다'예요.
explain_en: In daily talk people usually say '고민', while '번민' appears in writing and stories when the heart is truly troubled. It is common in '번민에 빠지다' (fall into anguish) and '번민이 깊다' (anguish is deep). The verb form is '번민하다'.

examples.en: He agonized for a long time before making the choice.

examples.ko: 혼자 번민하지 말고 저한테 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't suffer alone, please tell me.
There is no need to torment yourself over small things.
His mother worried anxiously about her son's future.
I agonized all night and finally made a decision.
The way he was tormented looked pitiful.

explain: '고민하다'보다 괴로움이 크고 무거운 느낌이라서 글이나 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '고민하다'나 '괴로워하다'를 쓰는 편이에요. '번민에 빠지다'처럼 명사 '번민'과 함께 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It feels heavier and more painful than '고민하다', so it appears more in writing and stories. In everyday talk people use '고민하다' or '괴로워하다'. Learn it together with the noun '번민', as in '번민에 빠지다'.

examples.en: Rabbits have very strong reproductive power.

examples.ko: 이 잡초는 번식력이 좋아서 금방 퍼져요.
examples.en: This weed multiplies well, so it spreads quickly.
Plants with weak reproduction are hard to grow.
The reproductive power of cockroaches is truly amazing.

examples.ko: 번식력 때문에 외래종이 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of their fast reproduction, foreign species are becoming a problem.
Mold multiplies fast, so you have to be careful.

explain: '번식력이 강하다/좋다/약하다'처럼 써요. 주로 동물, 식물, 곰팡이, 세균이 많이 퍼지는 힘을 말할 때 나와요. 끈질기게 살아남는 힘은 '생명력'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as '번식력이 강하다/좋다/약하다' (reproductive power is strong/good/weak). It mostly appears with animals, plants, mold and bacteria that spread quickly. The power to survive stubbornly is '생명력', which is a different word.

examples.ko: 번잡한 도심을 벗어나 한적한 시골길을 달렸어요.
examples.en: I left the busy city center and drove along a quiet country road.
This station is too crowded and hectic on weekends.
The market is hectic, but it is lively.

examples.ko: 차가 번잡한 시내로 들어서자 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: As we entered the busy downtown, the road got jammed.

examples.ko: 절차가 번잡해서 서류를 여러 번 냈어요.
examples.en: The procedure was troublesome, so I submitted the documents several times.

examples.ko: 번잡하지 않은 곳에서 조용히 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to rest quietly somewhere that is not hectic.

explain: 사람이나 차가 많아서 정신없고 어수선한 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요. 반대말은 '한적하다'예요. 절차나 일이 복잡하고 귀찮을 때도 쓰지만, 그냥 '복잡하다'보다 붐비고 번거로운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used for places that feel noisy and chaotic because of many people or cars. Its opposite is '한적하다' (quiet and peaceful). It can also describe procedures or tasks that are complicated and bothersome, with more of a crowded, hassle-filled feel than plain '복잡하다'.

examples.en: He is all smooth talk and his actions don't follow.
His face was shiny and greasy because of the oil.
I wore shoes with a glossy shine.
He is a person who is only shiny on the surface.

examples.ko: 번지르르 말은 잘하는데 믿음이 안 가요.
examples.en: He talks smoothly, but I don't trust him.

examples.ko: 손에 로션을 발랐더니 번지르르 윤이 났어요.
examples.en: After I put lotion on my hands, they became glossy.

explain: 반들반들 윤이 나는 모습을 말하지만, 실제로는 '겉만 번지르르하다', '말만 번지르르하다'처럼 겉이나 말만 그럴듯하고 속은 부족하다는 부정적인 뉘앙스로 많이 써요. 보통 '번지르르하다/번지르르한' 형태로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 겉만 번지르르하고 음식 맛은 별로예요.
phrases.en: This restaurant only looks good on the outside, and the food is not great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말은 그럴듯한데 알맹이는 부족할 때 비판하는 말투로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when the appearance or words sound impressive but the substance is lacking.

explain_en: It describes a smooth, shiny look, but in practice it is often used negatively, as in '겉만 번지르르하다' or '말만 번지르르하다', meaning it only looks or sounds good on the outside. It is usually used in the forms '번지르르하다' or '번지르르한'.

examples.en: I ate greasy food, so my lips are shiny with oil.
After I wiped the floor, it became glossy.
A child with a shiny face is smiling.
He put gel in his hair and combed it back sleekly.
The glossy shoes look brand new.
Your forehead is shiny from sweat.

explain: 기름기, 땀, 광택 때문에 표면이 윤이 나서 미끈해 보일 때 써요. '반짝반짝'은 깨끗하고 예쁜 느낌이 많지만, '번질번질'은 기름져 보이는 느낌이 있어서 때에 따라 덜 좋게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a surface that looks smooth and shiny because of oil, sweat or polish. '반짝반짝' often feels clean and pretty, but '번질번질' has a greasy look and can sometimes sound less positive.

examples.en: The children played in the stream with no clothes on.
After the wildfire, the mountain became bare.

examples.ko: 벌거숭이 땅에 다시 나무를 심고 있어요.
examples.en: They are planting trees again on the bare land.

examples.ko: 그 개울은 낮에 벌거숭이 아이들의 놀이터였대요.
examples.en: I heard that stream was a playground for naked kids in the daytime.
As a kid, I ran around like a little naked child every summer.

examples.ko: 나무를 다 벤 뒤 벌거숭이 산만 남았어요.
examples.en: After all the trees were cut down, only a bare mountain was left.

explain: 옷을 입지 않은 아이나 사람을 가리킬 때도 쓰지만, 요즘은 나무나 풀이 없는 '벌거숭이산'처럼 비유로도 자주 나와요. 산이 헐벗은 모습은 '민둥산'이라고도 해요. 사람에게 쓸 때는 주로 어린아이 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It can refer to a child or person wearing no clothes, but it often appears figuratively too, as in '벌거숭이산' (a mountain with no trees or grass). A bare mountain can also be called '민둥산'. When used for people, it is mostly heard in stories about small children.

examples.en: I was so tired that I flopped onto my back on the bed.
I fell flat on my back, but I wasn't hurt.

examples.ko: 그는 소파에 벌렁 드러누워 텔레비전을 봤어요.
examples.en: He lay sprawled on his back on the sofa watching TV.
I slipped on the ice and fell flat on my back.

examples.ko: 아이가 풀밭에 벌렁 누워 하늘을 봤어요.
examples.en: The child lay on his back in the grass and looked at the sky.

examples.ko: 벌렁 누워만 있지 말고 좀 일어나요.
examples.en: Don't just lie there on your back, get up a little.

explain: 등을 바닥에 대고 갑자기, 또는 아무렇게나 눕거나 넘어지는 모습에 써요. '벌렁 눕다', '벌렁 넘어지다', '벌렁 자빠지다'처럼 동작을 나타내는 말과 같이 나와요. 편하게 누운 모습이면 가볍고, 넘어진 모습이면 갑작스러운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes lying or falling with your back to the floor, suddenly or carelessly. It appears with action words like '벌렁 눕다', '벌렁 넘어지다' and '벌렁 자빠지다'. When someone lies down it feels casual, and when someone falls it feels sudden.

examples.en: I was startled and my heart pounded.
I went running and my heart is thumping.
He was angry and his nostrils were flaring.

examples.ko: 코가 벌렁거리는 걸 보니 화났나 봐요.
examples.en: His nose is flaring, so he must be angry.

examples.ko: 면접 전에는 가슴이 벌렁거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My heart was pounding before the interview, so I couldn't sleep.
My nose twitched at the delicious smell.

explain: '가슴이 벌렁거리다', '심장이 벌렁거리다'처럼 놀람이나 긴장으로 가슴이 크게 뛸 때 써요. 코를 크게 움직일 때도 '코가 벌렁거리다'라고 해요. 비슷한 '벌름거리다'는 주로 코나 콧구멍이 움직일 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used in '가슴이 벌렁거리다' and '심장이 벌렁거리다' when your heart beats hard from surprise or nervousness. It is also used for a nose that moves widely, as in '코가 벌렁거리다'. The similar '벌름거리다' is mainly used for a nose or nostrils moving.

en: widen and close alternately; flare; sniff

examples.en: The puppy sniffs, its nose twitching.

examples.ko: 아이가 코를 벌름거리면서 빵 냄새를 맡았어요.
examples.en: The child wiggled his nose as he smelled the bread.
He flared his nostrils as if he were angry.
The way the rabbit twitches its nose is cute.
He twitched his nose and then sneezed.

examples.ko: 소가 코를 벌름거려서 가까이 가기 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The cow was flaring its nostrils, so it was scary to go near.

explain: 주로 '코를 벌름거리다'처럼 코나 콧구멍이 넓어졌다 좁아졌다 하는 모습에 써요. 냄새를 맡거나 화가 났을 때, 숨을 크게 쉴 때 자주 나와요. 가슴이 뛰는 것에는 '벌렁거리다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in '코를 벌름거리다', for a nose or nostrils that widen and narrow repeatedly. It often appears when sniffing, being angry or breathing hard. For a pounding heart, '벌렁거리다' is more common.

examples.ko: 산에서 나무를 벌채하려면 허가를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: You need permission to fell trees on the mountain.

examples.ko: 무분별하게 벌채하면 산사태가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If trees are felled recklessly, landslides can happen.
The villagers cut down part of the forest.

examples.ko: 이곳은 벌채한 뒤에 새 나무를 심었어요.
examples.en: They planted new trees here after the logging.
The work of felling trees is dangerous.
You must not cut down trees without permission.

explain: '나무를 베다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 뉴스, 환경 이야기, 공문서에서 많이 나와요. 보통 숲이나 산에서 많은 나무를 베는 일에 써요. 집 마당의 나무 한 그루를 벨 때는 '베다'나 '자르다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '나무를 베다', so it often appears in news, environmental topics and official documents. It usually refers to cutting down many trees in a forest or on a mountain. For a single tree in a yard, '베다' or '자르다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 추석 전에 가족과 함께 벌초를 갔어요.
examples.en: Before Chuseok, I went to mow the grave site with my family.
I am going down to the countryside this weekend for grave mowing.
We finished tidying the graves early this year.
All the relatives gathered on the day of the grave mowing.
After mowing the grass, the grave looked clean.
My father does the grave mowing himself every year.

explain: 주로 추석 전에 조상의 산소에 자란 풀을 베고 깨끗이 정리하는 일을 말해요. '벌초하다'로 쓰고, 보통 '벌초를 가다/하다'라고 해요. 산소를 찾아가 인사드리는 '성묘'와는 달리, 벌초는 풀을 깎아 정리하는 일에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to cutting the grass and tidying up ancestors' graves, mostly before Chuseok. It is used as '벌초하다', and people usually say '벌초를 가다/하다'. Unlike '성묘' (visiting a grave to pay respects), '벌초' focuses on cutting the grass and tidying up.
